five_minutes: US 10-year Treasury yield surged to 4.79%, a high since January 2025, as rising oil prices reignited global inflation concerns.
Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey cautioned G20 members that energy shocks and volatile AI capex could trigger a global economic downturn.
UK long-term gilt yields climbed to their highest level since 1998 ahead of the October Budget, reinforcing global sovereign debt headwinds.
RBI stepped up liquidity absorption, pulling ₹4.60 lakh crore via overnight VRRR at a 5.24% cut-off rate to anchor money market rates.
US LNG exports expanded 23% in the first half of 2026 to 17.4 billion cubic feet per day, easing structural global gas supply tightness.

buckets.label: What you need to know today

items.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield surging to 4.79% tightens global liquidity and risks accelerating foreign capital outflows from Indian equities
items.what_happened: US 10-year Treasury yields rose to 4.79%, their highest level since January 2025, as crude oil price gains fueled fresh US inflation concerns.
items.why_it_matters: Higher US risk-free rates narrow the nominal rate differential with Indian G-secs, supporting the USD and pressuring the rupee. This tightens financial conditions across emerging markets and heightens FII withdrawal risks from Indian equities.
items.action: Revisit duration assumptions and currency hedge ratios across fixed income and equity portfolios.

items.headline: Bank of England G20 warning on AI capex and energy shocks firmed further after Governor Bailey flagged global downturn risks
items.what_happened: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey told G20 policymakers that energy market shocks from the US-Iran conflict alongside volatile AI technology investments risk forcing a broader economic downturn.
items.why_it_matters: This advances yesterday's G20 macro warnings, signaling growing worry among central bankers that input price shocks and uncertain technology capex returns will restrict global growth and delay central bank monetary easing.

items.headline: US LNG export surge of 23% in H1 2026 cushions global energy markets against Middle East supply disruptions
items.what_happened: US liquefied natural gas exports averaged 17.4 billion cubic feet per day in the first half of 2026, up 23% year-on-year, with H2 exports projected at 17.3 Bcf/d.
items.why_it_matters: Expanded North American natural gas export capacity offers a vital counterweight to global energy market volatility, containing imported energy price spikes for net energy importers.

items.headline: RBI overnight VRRR absorption expanded to ₹4.60 lakh crore as central bank tightens short-term banking liquidity
items.what_happened: The Reserve Bank of India absorbed ₹4,59,843 crore against a ₹5,00,000 crore notification via a 1-day VRRR auction at a weighted average rate of 5.24%.
items.why_it_matters: Following yesterday's ₹2.60 lakh crore drain, this second day of active liquidity management prevents excess banking system cash from dragging call money and overnight repo rates below the policy repo rate.

items.headline: RBI balance of payments Q1 FY27 breakdown provides view on capital flow drivers behind FX reserve movements
items.what_happened: The Reserve Bank of India published its foreign exchange reserve variation report for Q1 FY27 (April-June 2026) alongside official balance of payments statistics.
items.why_it_matters: Decomposing reserve changes between valuation effects and actual balance of payments flows shows how effectively foreign portfolio inflows and current account trends are supporting RBI's FX intervention buffer.

items.headline: UK long-term borrowing costs hitting 1998 highs highlights growing fiscal debt risk premiums across major G7 bond markets
items.what_happened: UK long-term borrowing rates escalated to their highest level since 1998 ahead of the government's October Budget announcement.
items.why_it_matters: Rising term premia in major sovereign debt markets reflect investor resistance to fiscal expansion, placing upward pressure on long-end global yields and elevating corporate refinancings costs globally.
